Mandate Capture Blueprint
Research note · 14 Nov 2026 · Version 2 · Public sources

What good mandate capture looks like

A scan of products, banks, open source and AI agents, turned into a feature list, entity-led functional journey and UX concepts for capturing and running account mandates.

Short answer. The reviewed evidence does not establish one product covering the whole mandate. The strongest ideas sit in four separate places: digital banks treat the signing rule as a self-service approval policy; Citi gives corporates one signer record across countries; one AI agent design checks the requested rule against the company registry; and open-source policy engines can evaluate the rule at payment time.

The feature list below combines them. The centre of it is a structured, versioned mandate that the form is generated from and that payments are checked against.

New in version 2
  • Reference journeys: the 28 inspected screens arranged against the 16 steps and product by product.
  • Botminds deep dive: company, agents, controls, UX patterns and limits.
  • New references: UK bank baseline, HSBC, Delega, Suomi.fi, Ramp and others; four rows added to Landscape and twenty-two sources.

Your evidence assessment

This is your local review of the source, not a vendor certification. Notes stay in this browser where storage is available.

Corrections that change the design

  • Mercury payment approval can count the requester. Qonto documents an optional separate four-eye control. The prototype’s preparer exclusion is our proposed policy.
  • Cygnetise shows personal sign-off limits and validity dates. Its full payment-rule execution semantics remain unverified.
  • Citi’s historical onboarding screens are not current Digital Signer Management screenshots. Country counts are dated coverage statements.
  • Fenergo’s public screens concern investor subscriptions into funds. They support an eSignature interaction pattern, not a complete bank-account mandate journey.
  • Botminds screens use sample data. Its independent reread and 95% threshold are vendor assertions, not independently validated performance.
  • No exhaustive search establishes that an open-source mandate product does not exist, or that other vendors lack a preview or rule tester.

Proposed solution design · not vendor functionality

16 steps, one shared case

Choose a step and an actor to see the screen, responsibility, handoff, control and trace that the ecosystem needs.

Design goal: collect once, route precisely, show the next action.

The customer administrator coordinates the organisation. The bank platform administrator configures systems. Neither automatically holds mandate-signing authority. Operations and RM views reuse the same case context, with permissions appropriate to each role.

This is a solution specification and interactive review model. Existing UX prototypes illustrate selected patterns; a production screen set for all roles has not yet been built.

All 16 steps × 8 actor views

Horizontal scrolling preserves the complete mapping. Every cell names a role-specific experience; “no task” avoids unnecessary handoffs.

Shared ecosystem and operating contract

One case, multiple workspaces

Customer portal, signer workspace, RM overview, colleague queues and platform console read the same versioned case. Keep entity, account, person and capacity separate. Reuse verified identity without inheriting authority.

One task owner

Task = case + entity/account scope + mandate version + person/capacity + requirement + accountable owner + assigned queue + due time + status + blocker + evidence references. Customer assignments require a named authorised representative. Specialist work routes by skill, jurisdiction, access and capacity.

Handoffs and parallel work

Scope → rule and roster → evidence reconciliation. Independent signer verification can run in parallel; signed execution waits for the approved frozen pack. Activation waits for approval and required receipts. Changes repeat only affected checks; the dependency graph still enforces every required gate.

Deterministic control, bounded agents

Agents propose extraction, explanation, impact and outreach. Workflow and policy services own state transitions. Capture source, prompt/model version and reviewer disposition. A high confidence score is not legal authority or an approval.

Tracking and observability

Use case, task, party, instruction, correlation and causation IDs. Emit versioned, idempotent events. Measure elapsed wait separately from active handling, queue age, failed dependencies, retries, rework and customer effort. Neutral external statuses protect restricted screening data.

Reduce friction deliberately

Batch evidence requests; nominate one communication owner; deduplicate reminders and triggers; retain context across RM/Ops; support assisted recovery. Customer sees the blocker, the person responsible and the next action. Service targets and escalation thresholds require agreed baselines.

Design sequence for the next iteration

First validate evidence and gaps. Then validate one fund case end to end across the eight views, including decline, expired delegation and failed activation. Extend the same components to the other entity profiles. Measure repeated questions, handoffs, waits and completion effort before choosing what to automate.

Target functional journey · by entity and authority

One reusable journey, with entity-specific authority checks. Select the customer’s underlying legal form, then establish who holds the account, who can bind that holder and who may operate it. This is a proposed coverage model, not a confirmed bank acceptance policy.

Which entities should we cover? · 15 journey profiles

These are routing profiles, not 15 mutually exclusive legal forms: funds and charities reuse the appropriate underlying form. Suggested build waves reflect reusable capability; prioritise with actual demand and risk.

ProfileProposed waveDistinct authority gate
Sole trader1 · CoreProve the individual-to-business link and any delegated authority.
Private limited company1 · CoreRequested rule must be supported by valid corporate authority.
Public limited company / listed company2 · Corporate complexityTrace treasury authority back to a valid corporate decision for this entity.
General partnership1 · CoreResolve jurisdiction, partner powers and contracting capacity before generating documents.
Limited liability partnership1 · CoreSeparate statutory/member roles from the particular authority being granted.
Limited partnership2 · Corporate complexityResolve LP legal personality and prove the full GP-to-person authority chain.
Trust / trustee-administered arrangement2 · Corporate complexityEstablish trustee capacity and distinguish beneficial interest from operating authority.
Club / society / unincorporated association2 · Corporate complexityConfirm the current officeholders and valid decision quorum/authority.
Incorporated charity / CIO / SCIO2 · Corporate complexityChoose the applicable jurisdiction and legal form before applying charity-specific requirements.
Registered society / cooperative / mutual3 · Specialist coverageConfirm incorporation and the correct governing/register framework.
Public / statutory body3 · Specialist coverageSpecialist approval of legal capacity and permitted activity before mandate setup.
Fund · corporate form2 · Fund coreMap the legal holder and governing body before accepting any delegated operator.
Fund · LP / private fund partnership2 · Fund coreEvery delegation edge must have evidence, permitted scope and effective dates.
Fund · unit trust2 · Fund coreResolve the division of powers; service-provider status alone does not confer signature rights.
Fund · contractual / co-ownership arrangement3 · Specialist coverageSpecialist-confirmed account holder and allocation of powers before signing.

Route by more than entity type

  • Legal form + jurisdiction: determines legal capacity and authority sources.
  • Business characteristics: fund, charity, regulated firm, listed company or SPV.
  • Relationship: direct, group treasury, agent/underlying principal or delegated operator.
  • Product + account: scope, currency, payment versus non-payment actions.
  • Lifecycle: new mandate, change, urgent suspension or periodic review.

Group, overseas branch, SPV, regulated FI, joint venture and agency are overlays, not substitutes for legal form. Resolve the branch’s owning legal entity; prove each principal’s delegation separately. Route unsupported jurisdictions to specialist review.

Keep three party questions separate

  • Who owns or controls it? Due-diligence parties and required checks.
  • Who can bind it? Governing body, trustee, GP or authorised delegate with evidence.
  • Who may operate this account? Named people or permitted agents within the approved mandate.

One party can have multiple roles. Being an owner, investor, director or service provider does not automatically make someone an account signatory.

Identify and check each party according to role and policy; not every related party becomes a separately onboarded customer.

Before step 1: confirm supported jurisdiction, underlying legal form, account-holder capacity and product scope. The selector below the heading adapts all 16 step details. The swimlane shows accountable ownership; identity, screening and evidence work can run in parallel where dependencies allow.

Select any step to inspect its entity-specific action, evidence, control and output. Additional specialist review is triggered by uncertainty in capacity, delegation or evidence.

UX Design · make authority understandable

Proposed screens for one connected mandate experience: customer admin, signatory and bank colleague. Fictional data; interactions demonstrate the concept and do not submit or activate anything.

Experience principles

  • Show the legal account holder and delegated role on every screen.
  • Reuse a person’s verified details; reconfirm authority for each scope.
  • Explain the rule in words and show what is still needed.
  • Save drafts, retain entered data after errors and offer assisted completion.
  • Use labelled controls, keyboard navigation and text with every status colour.

Patterns behind the design

Rule builder: Revolut / Mercury. Shared signer register: Citi / Cygnetise. Evidence and signing: onboarding platform. Conflict review: cited AI extraction. Enforcement: deterministic authority service.

Design synthesis from the existing blueprint, not screenshots or claims of available vendor functionality. The production workflow needs policy and service validation.

Journey Design · from intention to enforceable authority

Choose a scenario, then select a stage to see the customer experience, operational handoff and exit condition. Proposed service design mapped to the existing functional journey.

Service blueprint

Activation contract. “Approved” is not “live”. Show “Activation pending” until the authority service and required channels acknowledge the same version. Failed propagation holds affected instructions and creates an operations task; an emergency suspension follows its own authorised control path.

Botminds deep dive

What the Institutional Client Onboarding solution is, how its screens and agents work, what is proven, and what carries over to bank mandates.

Verdict. Botminds is the best public reference for the colleague's review workspace: one map of the case, narrow holds with a stated reason, cited agent reasoning, the source beside the extraction, and one plain request to the client. It is not a mandate product. It has no rule builder, no signatory classes or limits, no customer self-service and no activation into payment enforcement.

Everything below comes from the vendor's own pages and a demo that uses a fictional firm. No named customer, deployment or independent test of this solution was found.

What the solution does

It takes a won investment mandate at an asset manager from agreement to a funded account. The demo case is a Dutch pension fund placing $1.40 billion. Work runs on six lines with 21 stations, each dated backwards from the funding day.

AgreementKYC and AMLTax formsSigners and bank detailsCustody and accountsTrading setup

"Signers and bank details" is the line that matters for mandates. In the demo the registry lets the chair and secretary sign together, while the client's signatory list names three people and lets any one sign alone. One of the three has no authority at all. The agent holds only the stations that depend on this, explains why with page references, and drafts a single request for a board resolution.

The seven agents and what each must never do

AgentDoesNever
PlannerBuilds the map, dates stations back from funding, recomputes slack, chases owners, drafts client requestsMoves a funding date or contacts the client
KYCReads registry and entity documents in the original language, extracts cited values, compares the signing rule with the signatory listSets the final risk rating
ScreeningScreens sanctions, politically exposed persons and adverse media; rescreens nightly; proposes dispositionsCloses a match
TaxValidates tax forms line by line and checks expiryGives tax advice or accepts a failing form
SettlementChecks settlement instructions and signer authority; creates call-back tasks on an independent numberVerifies or releases bank details
Account setupOpens requests in downstream systems; codes guidelines into pre-trade rules with clause citationsSwitches an account live
CheckRe-reads every document blind on an independent model; sends disagreements to a person with both readingsAverages answers or overrides a person

Controls worth copying

  • Read, re-read, decide. One agent reads, a second re-reads blind, a named person decides anything with liability. The reader is never the checker and neither signs.
  • Person first below 95% confidence. The blind re-read runs on every document regardless of confidence.
  • Calibrated confidence. The platform says scores are calibrated per field against how often reviewed values were correct, refitted daily, with a blind audit sample of passing documents.
  • Separation of duties. Reviewer and approver must differ at every stage; refused attempts are recorded.
  • State-changing actions pause. Tools that send, write, move or pay wait for a person, who can approve, reject or edit.
  • Two-step client contact. A manager approves the request; a different person sends it.
  • Call-back on an independent number. The caller and the approver are different people. Changed details are held again.
  • Audit as a screen. Who, what, when, why, evidence and a hash, with one-click export of the file. Agent actions carry version numbers; human decisions carry reason codes.

How the platform says it governs agents

AreaWhat is describedWhat is not shown
Audit trailAppend-only entries, each sealed with a hash of the one before; a verify call reports the first broken entry; the customer can keep the latest seal outside the platformA sample export or the seal specification
SignaturesA signature is bound to a fingerprint of what was signed, needs re-authentication, and is marked superseded if a signed field changesEnforcement on every automated path
Change controlConfiguration snapshots with diff and rollback; agents, skills and prompts versioned separatelyRetention periods and defaults
EvaluationVersioned test cases with known answers; each case run several times and passed only if every run passes; a change is blocked if it regresses against a pinned baselineAny measured accuracy. The calibration table is labelled an illustration
RegulationControls mapped to the EU AI Act, the US model-risk guidance and the NIST framework. The page says it does not claim complianceThat the controls satisfy each obligation

What a bank's third-party risk review would still need: the SOC 2 report and ISO scope, a sub-processor and model-provider list, default data location and whether offshore staff can reach production, key management, recovery targets, breach notification terms, and audit and exit rights.

Where it sits, and how it measures itself

  • A layer, not a system of record. The vendor says a client lifecycle platform keeps the file and routes work, while the agents read, compare, chase and draft beside it. Nothing changes in a system of record without a person confirming. It offers an eight-week go-live plan.
  • Time to fund, not time to open. The headline measure runs from award to funded assets. In the sample, 71 days by hand against about 45 with the agents; both are illustrations for a fictional firm.
  • Where the days go in the sample: 20 waiting on the client, 15 on KYC and screening, 12 on signers, settlement instructions and call-backs, 11 on custody and trading setup, 10 on the agreement, 3 on tax.
  • Measures worth borrowing: waiting share by party, requests per customer, requests answered first time, holds per case with a cited reason, reader disagreements and days to resolve them, and slack to the target date.
  • One caution. The metrics page states a weekly cost of delay of about $160,000 for ten mandates; its own inputs give about $16,000. Treat vendor arithmetic as unchecked.

The vendor's own test list, reusable as acceptance tests

Botminds suggests eight checks before buying. Each one is a good test for any mandate agent:

  1. Plant a signer with no authority in a closed file.
  2. Plant a conflict between two documents.
  3. Check a passage in a foreign language against the original.
  4. Send a bank-details letter carrying a new phone number.
  5. Push a value just under the confidence threshold.
  6. Ask the agent to approve its own work.
  7. Change the model version mid-test and see what the log records.
  8. Export the whole file as an examiner would ask for it.

New references

Added in version 2. These fill three gaps in the first review: what UK banks offer today, shared signer registers, and registers where authority comes from the company registry.

The finding that shapes the design. Public digital mandate journeys stop exactly where complexity starts. Simple businesses change signatories in an app. Anything with more than two required signers, limits and panels, trusts, several accounts or higher turnover falls back to a PDF and an email. The gap between Business Banking and Corporate is a gap in the product.

Where the digital journey stops today

From public help pages read on 14 Nov 2026. These describe servicing changes, not onboarding.

BankDigital routeWhere it stopsFallbackStated time
NatWestMobile app: add, remove or amend signatories and third partiesSole traders, limited companies and companies limited by guarantee only; fewer than five accounts; signing rule needs no more than two signersOnline form up to £2m turnover; above £2m an on-screen PDF emailed to the service team, desktop only10 to 14 business days
BarclaysOnline mandate change form in Online Banking; view the mandate onlineComplex changes are sent to the phone linePost, signedAims for 14 days
LloydsA Full Access User adds or removes signatories and changes signing rules online or in the app; approvers get an email link and a text codeTrusts and pensions; signing rules with limits and panels; turnover above £25mTwo PDF forms for complex rules; above £25m email the servicing team for formsNot stated

Useful details: Barclays publishes who must authorise a change for sixteen entity types, from sole trader to embassy. Lloyds separates full signatories from limited ones, who can pay but cannot change the mandate. NatWest asks for a photograph of each signature. Lloyds needs a board resolution when the approvers have left.

Banks' own corporate tools

Bank portal · Bermuda page read

HSBC eSign on HSBCnet

System administrators add signatories and update mandate signatories inside the portal, with live status in the message centre. No paper or wet signature.

Limit: a mandate change does not change portal user permissions. Only the Bermuda page was read.

Treasurer peer group

What treasurers ask banks for

Real-time visibility of signers, data flowing by API into treasury systems, standard file formats, and a bank-agnostic option. Citi's tool updates signers; J.P. Morgan's shows and reports them but updates still go by email.

Limit: figures are from the peer group's write-up and are dated.

Source ↗
Platform vendor article

Backbase on agentic commercial onboarding

An entitlement agent drafts user roles, approval rules and limits from the client's mandate, and a person on each side signs off before go-live. Autonomy is set per task at three levels and is revocable.

Limit: does not say how signer authority is verified.

Source ↗

Signer registers shared between corporate and bank

Fintech · 2021 press release

Delega, with Deutsche Bank and Barclays

A proof of concept with eight multinationals. The corporate keeps one signatory list and shares it with chosen banks. Both sides see the same authority levels in real time, and the corporate sees which documents each bank requires.

Limit: a 2021 proof of concept. Current production use was not confirmed.

Source ↗
Treasury platform · undated

TIS with Delega

Delega supplies the screens for signatory rights across banks; TIS supplies bank connectivity. Data moves between the two by API.

Limit: no participating bank is named.

Source ↗

Registers where authority comes from the company registry

Government service · Finland

Suomi.fi e-Authorizations

Who may grant a mandate is read from the Trade Register. Where the company is represented jointly, one person starts the mandate and the other validates it. Mandates start now or on a future date, carry a status (valid, not valid yet, invalid), and can be filtered and exported.

Limit: no expiry reminders are sent. Foreign companies and unusual cases go to a manual application.

Source ↗
Government service · Norway

Altinn

Access follows a person's role in the Register of Legal Entities, and holders delegate rights onward.

Limit: page titles only; not yet read in detail.

Source ↗

Rule builders outside banking

Spend platform · help page

Ramp approval matrices

Each amount tier is a maximum and the lowest tier that covers the request wins. A sequential mode escalates through every tier up to the first with enough authority. A catch-all row guarantees an approver; an admin fallback is added if no tier is high enough.

Limit: no test or preview is described.

Source ↗
Spend platform · announcement

Brex policy rule builder

If-this-then-that rules over accounting, user and custom fields, with several rules in one policy and approval chains that route dynamically.

Limit: the page read gives no detail on testing or publishing.
